references.text: Matthew tells of Jesus by the Sea of Galilee, where he began to gather crowds and call disciples.
Jesus sits by the sea as large crowds gather around him to hear him speak, reflecting the crowd's pressure in Luke 5:1.
Mark's parallel account of Jesus by the Sea of Galilee where he calls his first disciples.
The crowd came to Jesus by the sea, and he taught them – paralleling the people's eagerness to hear God's word in Luke 5:1.
The crowd pressed in on Jesus so that he asked the disciples to keep a boat ready, reminiscent of the crowd's pressure in Luke 5:1.
Jesus began teaching by the sea, and a large crowd gathered, so he went out into a boat – closely paralleling the situation in Luke 5:1.
Just before this event, the crowds sought Jesus and wanted to hold him back, which explains the great crowd pressure in 5:1.
Again, a large crowd gathers from the towns to hear Jesus speak, a repetition of the pattern from Luke 5:1.
John mentions the Sea of Gennesaret (Sea of Galilee/Sea of Tiberias), the same lake referred to in Luke 5:1.
Matthew notes that Jesus and his disciples came to the region of Gennesaret, identifying the geographical location by the sea mentioned in Luke 5:1.
The Sea of Kinneret (Sea of Gennesaret) is already mentioned in the Old Testament and is the same lake as in Luke 5:1.
Faith comes from what one hears, and what one hears comes through the word of Christ – the crowd in Luke 5:1 pressed forward to hear precisely God's word.
